title: Define settlement correction, reversal uniqueness, and control-account projections
description:
References: §§5.6/5.7, 8.1/8.2, Appendix A/B/F (lines 419-423, 519-522, 536, 1165, 1241-1246, 1335, 1339).
Open amount = original minus summed SETTLES, but no immutable application-undo law is specified when a receipt or invoice is reversed/replaced. Reversing a settled receipt's GL legs leaves the invoice closed unless settlement effects reverse too; copying the original settles into the reversal can double-apply. Define versioned application effects and their bitemporal fold, target-side/unit validation, and over-application protection.
Acyclic SUPERSEDES plus exact target negation does not prevent two different idempotency keys from reversing/replacing one original twice. O + (-O) + (-O) is still acyclic and each reversal satisfies the local rule. Specify which reversal/replacement lifecycle actions are permitted and the concurrency witness; reversing a reversal must remain explicit if supported.
§5.6 says native detail postings inherently fold into the control account. The Register key schema has one account_ref, while only Leaf accounts accept legs. Define summary roll-up ownership, prohibit double counting and specify the externally fed detail-vs-summary representation so there is no second posting universe.
Acceptance: receipt applied then reversed; invoice replaced after partial application; concurrent duplicate reversals; two customers under an AR control account plus external-summary import. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.7 application effects versioned (open = original - SETTLES + UNSETTLES; reversals carry kernel-emitted unsettles; replacements re-declare, never copy); §8.2 reversal/replacement uniqueness by identity-derived vids (second reversal = AlreadyLive conflict; reversing a reversal explicit); §5.6 leaf-only register cells with rollup cells for summaries and external detail outside the book. FA-INV-08 clauses unsettle, reversed-once. Left open for re-review.

title: Define control-record encoding and immutable lifecycle projections
description:
References: §§4.2, 5.10, 7.3, 8.3, 10.2, Appendix A/C/F (lines 286-317, 435, 483, 540, 606-620, 1144, 1200-1207, 1278-1279, 1329).
Every Entry requires 2 or more posting legs, including SchemaControl/PolicyControl/PeriodControl in the same EntryClass union. Creating the first chart/calendar/book or opening a Future period has no legitimate pair of posting legs. Encoding invented zero-value accounting legs would violate the no-prototype/no-fabricated-leg doctrine. Define a journal record union or a precisely class-dependent payload with control effects separate from posting legs.
Lifecycle objects are declared immutable after commit (FA-INV-02), yet Period.state is a versioned property, RestatementCase/CloseRun/Finding/DraftSet carry changing status, Capability carries revoked, and §5.10 compare-and-sets membership counters. Specify which immutable transition records are authoritative and which current-state objects are disposable projections, with reconstruction and known-at rules. Attestations on a Register must bind its coordinate/value digest rather than merely a mutable/rebuildable cell identity.
Negative examples: create an empty book and first account without fake legs; transition case Proposed→Approved→Posted without updating its original payload; rebuild lifecycle state from immutable transitions. W1-W4, G0.
Model follow-up: entity-scoped capabilities and cash-by-legal-entity registers require an authoritative entity assignment. Entry/Account/Leg schemas and declared edges do not identify an owning LegalEntity, and the Dimension kind list has no mandatory legal-entity dimension. Either constrain each book to one declared entity or specify the balanced entity dimension and membership checks; do not infer ownership from descriptions.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.1 immutability model (payload objects / lifecycle-by-transition objects with projected status / rebuildable projections); control classes carry legs=[] and a typed ControlPayload union (Appendix A); FA-INV-02 clauses payload-immutable, lifecycle-by-transition, control-record; LegalEntity.code and Book.entities with legal_entity as a mandatory balancing dimension (per-entity clause of FA-INV-01, §5.2); RegisterEquals binds cell_key + fold_digest (§9.4). title: Specify N-leg hold resolution, reserved availability, and expiry-period behavior
description:
References: §§5.4/5.5, 7.6, Appendix A/B/C/F/G (lines 409-415, 495, 1175, 1242, 1268, 1342, 1374).
Posts { amount: Amount } generalizes a two-leg TigerBeetle transfer inadequately to N-leg/multi-unit holds. A pending USD entry D A60, D B40, C cash100 resolved for 60 admits D A60/C cash60 or D A20/D B40/C cash60, both balanced and under original legs. Neither schema nor law chooses. Multiple currencies cannot fit one Amount. Require a per-leg balanced subvector, named proportional law, or explicit registered absence.
Limit reads say head net balance but do not define worst-case reserved availability. With cash100, a pending outflow80 must block a second80 and an unrelated posted outflow30; pending inflow cannot finance an outflow before resolution. Specify reserve/consume/release equations and atomic witnesses.
Pending created in Open can encounter Closed/Locked before timeout. Appendix C allows only Voids in Locked, excluding Expires; §5.4 requires Expires for every elapsed deadline, so the sweep can become permanently inadmissible. Define origin-vs-posting-period routing, unconditional lawful reservation release, and close/lock preconditions.
A bounded sweep cannot both expire every due hold in one transaction and obey max_batch_entries for an arbitrarily large due population. Pin epoch/cursor/batch progression and visibility under backlog. Apply the same precision to scheduled reversals after the target period closes.
Acceptance: the N-leg ambiguity above; multi-unit partial; pending-spend race; locked-period expiration; sweep batch overflow; crash/manual-resolution interleavings. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.4 Posts{posted_legs} per-leg balanced sub-vector (scalar = two-leg sugar; ProportionalPost law), resolution unique by identity-derived vid (manual void vs sweep = AlreadyLive conflict), timeout measured from the TimeEvidence tick, reserved-availability equations (pending outflows reserve, pending inflows never finance), SweepCursor batching under max_batch_entries; Appendix C Pending/Resolution rows (Voids/Expires admissible except Future); Appendix A Disposition; Appendix B PostReserve. title: Close evidence-required and retention/erasure contract gaps
description:

Common intent evidence is optional and Entry.evidence has no minimum or class-specific source contract. A registered Intent origin with an empty evidence list satisfies the written unknown-reference check vacuously, contrary to AGENTS' rule that an entry without registered evidence is unencodable. Define required real evidence by class (manual assertion/control authority may be explicit objects), and distinguish drafts from committable entries.
External documents retain locator+observed digest, not necessarily bytes. FA-INV-05 promises strong retention of the provenance closure for the retention floor. Specify durable custody requirements or a downgraded, non-equivalent external-evidence profile with failure behavior; a URL alone cannot ensure retention.
AttachEvidence appends edges after commit but Entry.evidence is digest-covered and immutable. Separate original posting evidence from later supplemental evidence, version the latter and specify how each closure is selected/certified.
Erasure promises no PII outside Party/Document, but immutable descriptions, leg memos, tags, external IDs, source-entered-by fields and structured event data can carry PII. Specify schema-level sensitive-field placement and key granularity; erasing a Party alone cannot remove those copies. title: Preserve publication and historical identity in migration and scenario interim postures
description:
References: §§5.8, 8.6, 15.2, Appendix G/H (lines 427, 552, 833-835, 1371, 1376, 1395, 1402).
§5.8 promises staging followed by one atomic migration finalization. R-BULK's interim is ordinary committed WriteBatch chunks with manifests/resume; no staging visibility or finalization filter is defined. Readers may see an incomplete migration, and a later bad chunk cannot roll back already committed entries. Specify durable staging within the same engine, activation semantics and failure/retry visibility, without deleting history.
Scenario fallback replays trunk into a fresh open_memory database, whose assigned CommitSeq/HLC and allocated VIds differ. Entry digests embed book/branch/account identities, and approvals/certificates bind those digests. Pin original-coordinate provenance and identity translation or a read-only base-plus-overlay abstraction so replay does not forge recorded time or claim original membership. Replaying only accounting objects cannot reproduce physical sequences containing access logs/checkpoints/maintenance.
Close rehearsal needs computable draft balances before substrate branches exist, but §15.2 describes draft materialization as future optional and scratch replay only for scenarios. State the shared law for all draft report reads and for promotion changing head.
Restatement case posting is atomic in §8.3/§5.1 yet Appendix G allows a separate case-transition transaction. Place the entries and posted-state effect in one transaction or specify exact recoverable state and idempotency preventing repost.
Acceptance: invalid final migration chunk, crash around activation; scratch replay with intervening system records; draft-to-trunk digest/approval changes; crash after case entries before transition. W2-W4/W5, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §8.6 MigrationRun staging invisible until Finalize (Abandoned runs stay journaled and invisible; retries are new runs); §15.2 one scratch-book law for drafts and scenarios (accounting objects only, identity-derived vids and seq-free payloads preserve digests and approvals, SeqMap in the certificate, no forged membership); Appendix G restatement case post is one write_ordered transaction with its LifecycleTransition. title: Make unit evolution, signs, overflow, and FX residual laws mutually consistent
description:
References: §§4.4, 5.2, 6.1/6.4/6.7, Appendix A/F (lines 325, 395, 443, 455, 467, 1131-1132, 1145-1146, 1328, 1333).
1. Amount stores only unit_id and i128 mantissa. §4.4 allows changing that unit's scale and rescaling every stored mantissa, contradicting immutable entries and digests. Example: mantissa 100 means 1 at scale 2 and 0.1 at scale 3. Use immutable unit-version identity with a named conversion/migration law; never silently reinterpret or rewrite historical payloads. Distinguish precision changes from economic redenomination.
2. Entry legs have both Debit/Credit and signed i128 without a nonnegative-leg rule. Reversal wording says exact negation without deciding side swap vs signed storno. Negative legs can undermine per-side amount limits and produce two representations of the same posting. Define one canonical sign convention and boundary behavior, including i128::MIN.
3. Bounded checked i128 amounts are not an unrestricted ordered abelian group: MAX+1 and -MIN fail. Proofs/metamorphics need representability hypotheses or an unbounded reference domain; summation policy must define intermediate overflow and register cumulative totals.
4. FX residual encoding is incomplete: EUR debit 1 minor unit + debit 1 = credit 2; at rate 1/2 under HalfUp, USD base debits 1+1 != credit 1. Adding one USD credit residual fixes base balance but violates USD per-unit balance. Define lawful base-only valuation/residual effects or a complete balanced construction, including remeasurement and historical-cost release, without inventing funds or weakening FA-INV-01.
Acceptance must include these exact examples, inverse/cross-rate scale boundaries, negative refunds/allocations and both per-unit/base validation. W1/W2/W7, G0.

title: Specify public evidence commitments and scope-completeness proofs
description:
References: §§9.1/9.6, 11.11, 13.1-13.3, 15.6, Appendix A/F (lines 560, 580, 704, 745-755, 917, 1188-1194, 1217-1223, 1341).
The MMR is ordered by commit, whereas bundle scopes filter by effective period/account subtree, and retroactive entries make matching records noncontiguous. Inclusion proofs prove supplied leaves belong; they do not prove all matching leaves were supplied. Appendix A contains inclusion_paths but no range/selection-completeness proof, while the CPA workflow says fa-verify confirms a complete FY extract. A producer can omit one matching entry and all retained membership proofs still verify.
Define a sound supported proof mode (e.g. verify the full relevant prefix and selection or an authenticated predicate index bound to the same checkpoint), exact scope/known-at/auth intersection, missing-entry negative vectors, and accurate costs. Do not label membership_only as complete.
Document Oid uses the substrate's keyed identity (fgdb-crypto/src/lib.rs:80-97). A verifier with only public bundle/root cannot recompute it without K_oid. ImportReceipt.digest_at_receipt could provide a public binding, but its algorithm/domain and authenticated binding to Document Oid, kind, bytes and length are not specified. Require an explicit public body commitment chain without disclosing the storage key.
Whole-document hash alone also cannot verify arbitrary disclosed byte ranges against the original redacted document. Define chunk commitments or weaken the redaction proof scope honestly. Specify signature schemes, public trust anchors, key rotation and signed transcript; the std-only verifier budget must cover these implementations.
RFC scope reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html . W4/W9, G0/G1.
The canonical Entry deliberately excludes its creating MarkerRef/recorded time. An MMR leaf of only Entry bytes plus a checkpoint's aggregate commit_seq does not authenticate the per-entry commit sequence/HLC, especially when one commit has many leaves. Specify a domain-separated leaf envelope binding record kind, book/branch, creating marker/sequence, and within-commit ordinal, with canonical ordering and a proof of the sequence-to-prefix boundary used by historical selection.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §13.2 LeafEnvelope binding kind/coordinate/commit_seq/within-commit ordinal/selection fields; ScopeIndexComplete mode with scope_index_root in every checkpoint and boundary-neighbor proofs (missing-entry negative vectors); §9.1 public doc_commit over a 4 KiB chunk tree (substrate ObjectId is a locator only), redaction at chunk granularity labeled honestly; Ed25519 + TrustAnchorSet + KeyRotation in the std-only verifier budget; §13.1 completeness_scope labels; Appendix A LeafEnvelope/ScopeIndex/TransparencyCheckpoint/Bundle; FA-INV-14 clauses. Left open for re-review.

title: Remove approval and certificate hash cycles before freezing durable schemas
description:
References: §4.2/4.6, §10.1/10.4, Appendix A (plan lines 294-305, 333, 592, 645, 1128-1172, 1200-1223).
Entry BodyDigest excludes only entry_digest and includes approvals. ApprovalRef itself contains approved_digest. §4.6 requires that digest to equal the committed object's digest. Consequently d = H(entry containing approval.approved_digest = d), a cryptographic fixed point rather than a constructible approval flow. RestatementCase similarly embeds approvals and mutable lifecycle status. Attestation and checkpoint signature transcripts also lack explicit exclusions of the signatures and signed-digest fields.
Certificate/output references have a related missing contract: Finding contains certificate_oid and the certificate contains output_digest of the result; bundles contain report certificates; Origin::Intent contains plan_certificate_oid. Without a distinct semantic output body, hashing can become cyclic or depend on runtime IDs/approvals and make Canon's byte-for-byte replay claim impossible.
Required repair: an explicit acyclic identity/transcript graph separating immutable proposal digest, approvals/signatures, committed envelope digest, and certified semantic output. Bind approvals to complete effects, book, target coordinate and policy epoch; require reapproval if promotion replays materially different effects. Enumerate ordered construction and digest tags for every signed/certified type. Negative acceptance: change one leg after approval must fail, while adding the first valid approval must be constructible without finding a hash fixed point. W1/W3/W4, G0.

Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.6 acyclic identity graph (EntryProposal -> proposal_digest -> plan certificate -> Approvals binding proposal_digest+effects_digest+coordinate+policy epoch -> envelope entry_digest); Appendix A Entry/Approval/Attestation/Checkpoint transcripts exclude signatures/self-digests; normative construction order added; RestatementCase split into immutable body + projection with Approval objects; negative acceptance stated (leg change after approval => digest mismatch refusal; first approval needs no fixed point). title: Bind commit authorization and audit delivery to explicit current policy
description:
References: §§5.1/5.10, 9.7, 14.2-14.4, Appendix A/G/H (lines 375-386, 435, 584, 779-787, 1224-1225, 1365-1375, 1399).
Plan has initial admission and commit-time SoD but no explicit current-policy witness for revocation/expiry between dry run and commit, or for reads pinned before revocation. known_at should select accounting history without resurrecting revoked access. daily_total and per-entry amount ceilings require a precise measure (gross debit, credit, absolute per-leg, per-unit), day/time-zone source, shared principal/token scope and serializable budget debit. Net of balanced entries is always zero. Attenuation/issuance must not reset a principal ceiling. No operation-cost row prices those stateful checks.
Every external-profile read must be completely logged, but Appendix G declares balance/report/bundle reads 0 writes. Define durable access recording before protected bytes escape, stream/cancellation/failure semantics, daemon authority for read-only callers, and avoidance of recursive log reads. Price the real transaction/barrier or name a distinct admitted audit path.

2. Upstream changes are fine: file GitHub issues with the requests (nine filed, listed below).
3. Adoption follows a concrete consumer slice (plan rule): each adoption bead lands the pin in the same change as the first consuming code.

METHOD: four read-only explorer passes (no builds), each reading README/plan/architecture headers, root Cargo manifests, crate counts, .rs counts, #[test] counts, status notes and last commit dates; verdicts are tied to file paths.
